column8: Sun 22 Nov: 3b or Table 3 row 7's note: maintenance of value is the exact name for IPS l.15's 'a stronger Taiwan dollar' (read at source); ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 3 holds it as a reserve fact, not 3b's parallel, and 3d's one outside parallel is Spelman, so it lands only if it wins aha test 9 (Mon 23 Nov); never in Laura's words.

Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 7: IDA's duty ended once the money was spent or exchanged, the same end date as her flexibility's currency job (the day the residency changes her dollars); a reserve fact behind row 1.
Sun 22 Nov: Store, behind row 1: IDA's clause ran both ways; hers is one-way and capped, which is why it is an intention, never a promise (3b).

Sun 22 Nov: 3b or 3d, one clause if row 1 lands: even IDA switched maintenance of value off in 2022 (IDA20 para 6(d), read at source), so her top-up can only be an intention with a known size; reserve fact otherwise.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: IDA fixes its rates on a six-month average before pledging; for one donor the dated central-bank closing rate (store Q26-025, Q10-024) does the same job.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: the receiving fund hedges after pledges are counted; supports the rule that her flexibility is money held back, never a hedge.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d: one named day's rate for every pledge (Global Fund, via a secondary report of the committee decision), so her NT$ value is given at the rate on the day she states her figure; source a report, not the FX framework itself.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: the Global Fund's averaged rate for late pledges over 20 million dollars; one-figure donor, no use in the report.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: hedge, reserve or bear; the Fund hedges, her plan holds no derivatives, so her flexibility is a reserve; never call VT or her flexibility a hedge against the Taiwan dollar.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: careful funders count a foreign-currency pledge below face (size unstated); the dated NT$ value plus a stated intention is Keel's reading, not a finding.

Sun 22 Nov: Store or Table 3's note: the Global Fund's Swiss-franc budget lost about a tenth, the ten payments' currency problem at scale; 3e's one outside parallel is the 2022 gilt crisis (ARGUMENT_TREE), so not in 3e's prose.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d: gift offices count foreign money at its value on the day it arrives (CASE A.4.1), so only the US-dollar figure is fixed before the residency changes the money; known practice.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d, behind Q200's signed letter: CASE counts a pledge only with documents confirming size and timetable; that the size includes its currency is Keel's reading (row 17).
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Carnegie Mellon values foreign currency on the day received; a US university, supports row 12.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Fordham puts conversion cost and timing on the donor by default; why her letter says who changes the money (store Q69-042).
Sun 22 Nov: Store: a fourth gift office counting on arrival; adds nothing to row 12.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d: no gift-office policy read covers a pledge written in a foreign currency, so the currency clause must sit in her letter; Keel synthesis of four policies, not a survey.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, one clause at most: Taiwan's Ministry of Culture counts foreign money at the rate obtained and asks for the bank's exchange slip, so the 2031 NT$ figure is an illustration; say it is a community-grant settlement form, not the capital-grant rule.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Ministry-supervised foundations keep NT$ books; the residency's legal form is outside the case (l.169), so background only.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d candidate turn: ink in her ledger, pencil in theirs (IAS 21 retranslation); competes with 3d's existing turn (the team says before her words that the page shows only ink), one turn per part, never in Laura's words; the IAS 21 citation would be a second outside reference in 3d, so the turn must stand without it.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d's currency clause, its reason (D9): ink only in the currency the promise is paid in (FAS 76, Q173-003) and nothing she holds pays Taiwan dollars, so she states US dollars; a NT$ figure would be pencil the day she said it.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d's dated illustration: $115,000 is NT$3.77m at 32.768 on 6 Nov 2026, NT$3.43m 10% stronger, NT$3.16m at 27.52, all NUMBERS 8j; never a NT$ figure without its day.

Sun 22 Nov: 3b or 3d (D9): about $11,500 keeps her own contribution's NT$ value whole after a 10% stronger Taiwan dollar, 10% of $115,000, never of the building; her flexibility alone covers it in about 93 of 100 (NUMBERS 8j 92.9%); kept over its near twin Q201-027, which says 1 in 20 from overlapping windows and all she keeps.

Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 7's note or 3e: fix, drop '1-in-20 +13.7%' (417 overlapping windows; D7, never 1 in 20 from overlapping windows); give the largest two-year move (+29.4%, 1986-88) and 98.3% as a share of windows, never as odds; figures match NUMBERS 8j.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's clause for campaign director 34 (D9): fix, the tenth-to-a-fifth spread across ten Januaries is Keel arithmetic on the FRED mirror, not in NUMBERS; register it in NUMBERS 8d or 8j before 27 Nov, else say only that the ten are fixed in US dollars so their NT$ value moves.
Sun 22 Nov: Store only: fix, the since-1984 spread (10.0% to 59.9%) is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS; never in prose unless registered.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's one clause (D9): the case fixes the ten in US dollars and the IPS names her flexibility for the building (l.15), so programme funders carry the payments' NT$ move; she promises nothing after 2033.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d funder line: fix, 'its bad years she meets from money kept back' reads as a promise from money promised to no one; say she means to meet a stronger Taiwan dollar from her flexibility, as far as it goes (row 29's 'means to'; IPS l.15; D9).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d's currency sentence (D9): fix, 'because that is what her Treasuries pay' becomes 'because the Treasury fund that pays it pays US dollars' (D2: the top is paid by a Treasury fund holding Treasuries maturing in 2032, never called Treasuries), and 'an extra gift' becomes 'an extra contribution' (WORDS l.31).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, Laura's words for the voice writers: fix, 'the Treasuries I hold will pay' becomes 'the Treasury fund I hold will pay' (D1's form: held in Treasury funds), and 'paid in December 2032' becomes 'at the start of 2033' (WORDS l.31; the fund pays mid-December 2032); keep 'I mean to', never 'I will'; her whole commitment ($615,000) comes earlier in her words (D12).
Sun 22 Nov: 3d guard list: never 'I will make up any difference', never a NT$ figure without its day, 'exact' only with 'in US dollars', never a hedge; fits WORDS and D2.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d (D9, SD-1): her side of the sum is exact in US dollars, and in NT$ only on the day the residency changes the money; the one-total argument in its true unit.
Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 7: the base and end dates are Q69-043's three items; the reason the end date ends her duty is row 2's.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d: AFP's advance or nucleus gift names what her figure is, first committed before anyone else is asked, the profession's reason for SD-3's one clause 'first to commit, in writing'; said in plain words, never 'advance gift', 'gift' or 'lead gift'.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d's word choice: a leadership or pace-setting gift sets a standard against a goal, which the case does not set (l.164-166), so the report never says 'lead gift' (D12); store reason.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d: AFP's nucleus fund is the case's three jobs for her figure (l.110-112) in the profession's words; the role, with Q200's signed letter making it countable.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, one clause: measure her figure against her means, not a goal; fix, '25.6%' and 'about a quarter of the $450,000 she deposits' are Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS: register in NUMBERS 8w or drop, and say 'what she deposits', never her means (case l.61-63).
Sun 22 Nov: Store, WORDS' reason behind 'never lead gift': a gift range table needs a goal, and the case sets none.

Sun 22 Nov: Store only: fix, the 17-33% shares are Keel arithmetic on four US campaigns and the $575,000-$1.15m campaign size is Keel arithmetic on $115,000 at 10-20%, neither in NUMBERS; never in prose (the report simply never says 'lead gift').
Sun 22 Nov: Store: token and sacrificial gifts show the profession judges a founder by capacity; her capacity beyond the portfolio is not in the case.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d (D11): AFP's tripod puts the case for support with the residency; the team's draft is the leadership leg, so purpose takes one or two sentences from the case's facts and no more.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d: cumulative giving is the profession's word for a whole commitment, the reason to say the sum once, about $615,000 (NUMBERS 8w; D12), with its years.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: AFP's entry for asking one donor for an annual and a capital gift; headword unverified, no use.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d: CASE counts a comprehensive campaign (running money plus building) apart from a special-purpose one, so her words give each part with its purpose.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: CASE's counting of documented pledges, already in Q18-006 (2024 full, formerly five years); the six-of-ten, $300,000 count is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d: face value is not today's value; say '$50,000 a year, 2033-2042' so no co-sponsor reads $500,000 as cash in hand in 2031 (the ten cost $302,287 on 6 Nov, NUMBERS 1).

Sun 22 Nov: 3d, ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 5's reason for her whole commitment in two parts: Artists Rep's 2025 building budget carries $500,000 of operating seed funds for two years once open; an evidence clause, not 3d's one outside parallel (Spelman), always with 'a base, not the residency's whole budget'.
Sun 22 Nov: Store, behind row 14: a second campaign that budgets opening support as part of the project.

Sun 22 Nov: 3.0 or 3d: she has bought the line campaigns most often fail to raise after opening; Q202-020 already carries it in funders' words, with row 14 as the campaign evidence; never 'covers the decade'.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d's order (D12): parts first, then the sum once; fix, '$95,000-$115,000 for the building' becomes '$115,000 for the building', with $95,000 said once as the part held since January 2028 (D1: one form, never a two-number range in her words), then 'about $615,000' (NUMBERS 8w).

Sun 22 Nov: 3.0 or 3d: NCAF's 2026 budget form shows a founder's yearly payment as one income line among many, 'a base, not the whole budget' in a Taiwanese funder's own form; NT$1.64m only with its day (32.768, 6 Nov 2026).
Sun 22 Nov: 3d's order (D11): Taiwan's national arts funder asks for origin and purpose first and the finance plan third; the reader's habit, not a rule for her letter.
Sun 22 Nov: Store, behind row 19: a second Taiwan funder that puts purpose before budget.
Sun 22 Nov: Store or 3d's purpose sentence: affluent US donors give for the mission first (58%); motive, not reading order, and not Taiwan's programme officers.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d's order (D11): a founder's own launch words run vision, then her figure, then others; Laura's purpose sentences come from the case's facts, never invented quotations.
Sun 22 Nov: Store, behind row 22: the speaker is the executive director, not the lead donor, so weak support.

Sun 22 Nov: Store, one clause in 3d at most: project lenders accept equity paid last when something solid stands behind it; if used, say paid at the start of 2033 from a Treasury fund held for her (D2), never 'from Treasuries she already owns'; 3d's one parallel is Spelman.

Sun 22 Nov: Store, refused for use: its use for Laura is SD-6 ('her word takes the Treasury's credit'), which ATTACKS D8 dropped; the true half (late equity needs a backup guarantee) is row 24's break and Q200's signed letter.

Sun 22 Nov: 3b and 3d (D10): project lenders ask sponsors for contingent equity against overruns, and her flexibility is the opposite, promised to no one (IPS l.15), so co-sponsors count her stated figure and nothing for overruns; a contrast clause, not 3b's outside parallel (ARGUMENT_TREE: none needed).
Sun 22 Nov: 3d guard: 'first' means first committed, never first to absorb losses; overruns are the project's (D10).
Sun 22 Nov: Store: AFP's quiet phase and CASE's counting of it; the case puts first approaches in 2031 (l.109), so the timing point is row 29's.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d and FACTS_PLAIN (D12): the bottom can guide her planners from January 2028, the top after the move; fix, drop 'never changes' (D2 struck it: an early fund end at zero interest), say 'paid by a Treasury fund held for her' not 'held in Treasuries', 'the top is held from the move' not 'owned' (WORDS: she owns fund shares, never a figure), and D12's 'no figure above the bottom' not 'no top'; older twin H4-042 says owned and locked.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d (D12): 'at least $95,000' goes to the residency's own planners only; co-sponsors hear the figure once, after the 2031 move, since an early bottom anchors (Q147-037) and beating it earns little (H7-063).
Sun 22 Nov: Store only: the case's pull quote is the case's text, not Laura's; never as her words, and a slogan risk.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a, ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 2's reason before the price: a forward rate can be locked in only by someone who can both borrow and lend at it (Shiller and co-authors 1983, read at source); Laura only lends, so zero is the one rate on waiting cash she can count on.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a and 2.3 (D13's SB-1): with coupon bonds and no borrowing, certainty is bought by over-funding, and the $36,774 of extra Treasuries (NUMBERS 2) is the price of the lock she cannot buy; the sentence is the team's, never a judge's.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a or 3e's first-use definition: a forward rate is a break-even rate; use only the break-even reading (the lock by extending maturity needs a bond with no coupons, which she does not hold).

Sun 22 Nov: 3e and WORDS (D14): under liquidity preference forward rates are an upwardly biased estimate of expected rates (CFA), the textbook reason to say 'implied by today's prices', never 'expected'.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a: a coupon bond's yield assumes coupons reinvested at that yield, so each bond pays what it says (IPS l.13) while the ten's $50,000 each still needs its coupons to earn something; textbook.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e, one clause with row 7: the Philadelphia Fed's 32 forecasters, the week trading froze, put bills at 4.1%, 3.9% and 3.5% for 2027-29 (read at source); forecasters' expectations, never the forwards'.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's aha candidate: fix, the one-year forwards 4.66%, 4.70% and 6.07% and the 0.2, 0.7 and 1.1 point gaps are Keel arithmetic on the engine, not in NUMBERS (only 8a's 4.67% and 5.43% averages and the 2027 4.34% carry are); register before use, and name the bill-against-note adjustment.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: February 2026's ten-year survey (bills 3.00%, 10-year 4.00%) sits below 2033-42 forwards; taken before 2026's rise in yields.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e: beyond three years term premiums are the main driver of yields (Crump, Eusepi and Moench 2018), exactly where her coupons wait.
Sun 22 Nov: Store or a 3e note: the exact definition of the forward term premium, if the report names it once.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: a New York Fed line that the expectations hypothesis dramatically fails; row 4 already carries the wording change.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e: forecasters miss too (up to two points), so the report never swaps forwards for surveys; zero needs neither forecast.
Sun 22 Nov: 3a, behind row 14: futures' excess returns were strongly countercyclical, 3-5 times higher in recessions (Piazzesi and Swanson 2008).

Sun 22 Nov: 3a, one clause if Branch 2's budget allows: right before recessions futures kept forecasting high rates, so forward rates miss most in the recession IPS l.9 already fears for her career; finance's own literature (D6); horizon months, hers years.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Federal Reserve Board staff subtracted a premium before reading futures as forecasts; old convention, colour.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e: futures and swap rates 1990-2021 systematically exceeded the short rates that came, so 'expected' fails whether the gap is premium or error.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a, with row 14: the large misses came with crashes and falling share prices, so a reinvestment gap filled from her flexibility would sell low (NUMBERS 2 item 4), and zero avoids it; say 'her flexibility', never 'the half of VT kept', and never as shares paying a payment.
Sun 22 Nov: 3a or 3e: 1990-2021 the big surprises were cuts, the direction that hurts waiting money; always beside row 19 (it broke in 2022).
Sun 22 Nov: 3e honesty clause: in 2022-23 forwards underestimated tightening, so the case for zero is the timing of the big misses, never that rates always fall; authors not read.

Sun 22 Nov: Store or 3a if idea 1 is cut: waiting cash is the floating side that has lost on average, and the extra Treasuries move it to the fixed side; the record behind Q64-034's theory, a direction, never a size.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Cochrane and Piazzesi's tent-shaped factor, re-read; Q64-003 holds it.

Sun 22 Nov: Store or Table 2's note: a year ahead the forward spread is reward, not a forecast; fix, the 4.66% 2028 forward is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS (4.34% is only as NUMBERS 4's 2027 carry); register before use and never imply January 2028 yields are forecast higher.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Campbell and Shiller's abstract wording; Q64-002 holds the finding.
Sun 22 Nov: Store or a 3e note: Shiller's 'seems worthless' for the slope as a forecaster; colour behind rows 1 and 4, no Nobel line.
Sun 22 Nov: Store only: Macaulay's 1938 doubt, quoted at second hand; the book was not read.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: since 1962 forwards above later yields, two eras not 657 tries; reproduces Q64-011 within 0.1 point.

Sun 22 Nov: Store only: fix, the slope buckets (1.11 points 57%, 2.00 points 82%) are Keel arithmetic on FRED not in NUMBERS; never in prose; the report rests the zero standard on rows 1-20, not slope.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: the bond judge's curve was 25 Sep's; if attack 8 is ever answered, use the freeze-day curve.

Sun 22 Nov: WORDS and FACTS_PLAIN (D14): 'the rates implied by 6 November's prices (forward rates)', defined once as a break-even, and 'the same as a flat 5.12% a year on every waiting dollar' (NUMBERS 8a), never 'every coupon'; the fix for NUM-001.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a (D14): IPS l.11 is the promise and paid even if cash waiting earns nothing is the report's measure, because otherwise only her shares could fill a low-rate gap; fix, drop 'about 8% of her $450,000' (Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS) and price it as D14 and Branch 2 do ($36,774 of extra Treasuries; $39,162 with the top-up, about a quarter of the 2028 deposit).

Sun 22 Nov: Table 2's note or 3a, one clause (D14): fix, $33,460 is NUMBERS_ANSWERS' figure, not NUMBERS.md's, and 'barely moves' omits that pooling all cash would lift the central range one step, clearing it by only $523 (ATTACKS, answers that came back); say only the method: each of the ten with its own interest, only the extra Treasuries shared.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e at most: the replay's method (history's moves applied in proportion to today's forwards, assuming no premium) is Q64-015's, the 67.2% Q64-018's; D14 already carries the corrected wording from this card.

Sun 22 Nov: 3c and Table 2's note: the range is a reading on the curve of 6 November 2026, never on expected rates; the 13 Nov curve ($105,000-$125,000) and rates 3 points lower ($75,000-$95,000) are NUMBERS 4 and 8i register notes, never a re-size, and never a two-number range in Laura's words.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a's price sentence: about $46,600 coming back (NUMBERS 2, 1 Jan 2033 money) is the forward-rate case; at a flat 4% the ten as bought fall $13,906 short (NUMBERS 8a); say which rates each figure assumes.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, the name D4 and ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 1 ask for: background risk (Kimball 1993), a risk she cannot sell makes any other risk less welcome, even an unrelated one; abstract read at source, paraphrase it.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3's plain words for background risk: risks should tend to crowd each other out (Kimball 1991); keeps IPS l.9's conclusion without its weakest premise.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, one clause at most: proper risk aversion; once the ten are insured by Treasuries, money promised to no one can take share risk (IPS l.11); abstract only.
Sun 22 Nov: Store or References: Gollier and Pratt's risk vulnerability, the source of 'the tempering effect of background risk'; technical, out of prose.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: background risk argues for caution only when caution eases with wealth (not CARA); draft text.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: people with uncertain incomes are measurably more averse (Guiso and Paiella, one Italian survey, 2001 draft).
Sun 22 Nov: Store: the first household test of background risk (Guiso, Jappelli and Terlizzese 1996); abstract only.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 guard: for wage earners background risk trims shares by about 2 points, so it never explains a book 89.55% in Treasuries (NUMBERS 8g); the payments' certainty does.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, one clause: riskier income, even with no market link, shrinks the room for shares toward a retired investor's (Viceira 2001), the reply to the bond judge's bond-like-career argument; adds the key clause to Q1c-025.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: the textbook's answer to income risk is to save more; the case fixes her saving, so the plan's lever is the order of purchase (Keel inference).
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Campbell and Viceira's draft wording of row 9's point.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 or 3e: CGM's lower bound gives aha 2 a finance pedigree; the payments need only the deposit's first $39,162 (26.1%), so it could arrive 73.9% smaller (NUMBERS 5, 8u).
Sun 22 Nov: 3e or store: a cut to 10% of income counts almost as zero (CGM); the plan splits a smaller deposit (building money shrinks) from a missing one (IPS l.17); adds to Q33-018.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3: business income is the background risk that bites (more volatile, more linked to shares than wages), and Laura is a business owner (case l.44-45); a survey's summary, no figure.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3: the no-link studies leave out the self-employed (Q1c-026) while business owners hold less in shares (Q1-021), so the report answers 'your own evidence shows no link' without overclaiming.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 (D4's citation): Heaton and Lucas (2000a) for the idea that business income is a background risk, never for a number; abstract only.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: BMS's labour flexibility as insurance is Q39-003's quote; the perfectly hedged wage adds nothing the report uses.
Sun 22 Nov: Store or 2.3 clause: BMS themselves expect less risk-taking for a very risky wage; working-paper wording.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, one clause at most: a writer's extra work has no buyer in a slump (HMH's frozen acquisitions, cut speaking budgets, 2020's cancelled talks), so BMS's insurance is weakest when it would pay.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3: by the month 2020's share crash (-33.9% in 33 days, S&P 500) and the cancellations came in the same weeks, so Q1c-010's calendar-year counterexample does not show the two parting; 'can', no beta.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 1): same shock, slower clock, the honest reading of l.9's 'same period'; fix, for 2020 use the Census -12.4% for independent artists, writers and performers (Q1c-010), never the IRS sector's -23.4% or its 2021 recovery (arts, entertainment and recreation, gyms included, Q148-016, Q148-018: the -11.6% error of D4 again); 2009 stays -7.8%; 'can', never together.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3: the writers' 2009 figure is Q148-005's -7.8%; the correction is already in ATTACKS D4 and ARGUMENT_TREE (Sun 22 Nov), and SKELETON 3e note 4 still to fix on 27 Nov.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: PRH stretched 2020 advances rather than cancelling; Q12-004 holds it, the instalment percentages are second-hand.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: advances paid in three to five instalments are Q12-001's; the 2009 quarters add colour only.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: in 2009 delivery and acceptance clauses became the cut; agents' accounts with no counts.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: Australian royalties held better than event money in 2020; not her market.
Sun 22 Nov: Store: European writers' bodies expected postponed publication and money in 2020; organisations' expectations, secondary report.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3: Treasuries cannot hedge a career; what the plan removes is the payments' dependence on it (from January 2028 nothing more, before then the deposit's first 26.1%, NUMBERS 8u); 'hedge' only as the IPS's quoted word, never 'natural hedge'; sharper than Q33-024.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, aha 2 (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 1 uses it): the plan settles the background risk before taking share risk, no shares in 2027 and VT bought only with what the deposit leaves; fix, '42% less' is Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 5's $17,087 against $29,594, not printed in NUMBERS: register it in NUMBERS 5 or give the two figures.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3's frame for the 27 Nov writers (D4): paid in pieces, later and smaller in 2009 and 2020, named background risk, never beta; 'can', dated.
